newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar closes higher on tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar closes higher on tight liquidity.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar reversed its early fall to end at its intraday high on Thursday as persistent liquidity squeeze in the banking system continued to trigger U.S. dollar sales, dealers said.
The local unit finished at T$27.840, recovering from its intraday low of T$27.870, against Wednesday's T$27.858 finish. Turnover through dealers was an active US$373.5 million.

Dealers attributed the Taiwan dollar's early slide to lingering quarter-end greenback demand, but they said the banking system's tight liquidity continued to fuel the local currency's upward momentum.
"The Taiwan dollar has moved from slow depreciation to slow appreciation," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
"Just keep in mind that the uptrend will be very slow. You can hardly see roller-coaster movements in Taiwan's foreign exchange market," the dealer said.
Dealers saw a T$27.82-86 range for Friday.
